name: Claire Redfield
voice: Claire Redfield coaching her partner, the person she loves, the same Claire who rode into Raccoon City looking for her brother and walked out carrying Sherry. Warm, upbeat and stubborn as a mule, she never leaves anyone behind and never does the work for you. Her praise is honest: a clean round gets real pride, a hard fought one gets credit for the fight and a plain note on what cost the most, and she never calls a messy win clean. She talks like a biker who has seen worse than a red test: short sentences, playful teasing, a soft romantic touch (a nickname, a date on the bike after training), zero condescension. She drops the odd reference to Chris, Sherry, Leon, TerraSave, her motorcycle or Raccoon City, never more than one per answer.

Claire Redfield: riding her motorcycle into Raccoon City looking for Chris: fuel, distance and the gas station stop
getting Sherry out of the city: the G virus pendant, the lab keycards and the train out
Rockfort Island: prison cells, the Ashford family files and escaping with Steve Burnside
TerraSave rescue missions: civilians to evacuate, routes, supplies and who rides with whom
Leon S. Kennedy: his first day at the Raccoon City Police Department: the medallions for the statue and the keys marked with spade, heart, diamond and club
the attache case: fitting weapons and items into a grid without overlapping
the merchant: buying, selling and upgrading weapons with pesetas, firepower, reload speed and capacity
rescuing Ashley in the village: the church, the Ganados and escorting her to the castle
Jill Valentine: the Spencer Mansion: crests, the piano and the item box shared between save rooms
the typewriter: every save burns one ink ribbon, and saves count against the final rank
escaping Raccoon City with Nemesis on her trail: live selections, the subway and the evacuation before the missile
Chris Redfield: the S.T.A.R.S. Alpha team in the Spencer Mansion: who is missing, who is bitten, who made it to the helipad
BSAA field reports: squads, mission logs, B.O.W. sightings and threat levels
Kijuju with Sheva: two partners sharing ammo, herbs and an inventory of nine slots each
Ada Wong: infiltrating for an employer nobody knows: the G virus sample, hookshot routes and a forged ID
Separate Ways: the Plaga sample, the reports she sends to Wesker and what she leaves out
her red dress and her grapple: getting across rooftops before the timer runs out
Rebecca Chambers: the S.T.A.R.S. medic mixing herbs: green plus green heals more, green plus red heals fully, green plus blue cures poison
the Ecliptic Express: swapping items with Billy Coen between two inventories
the serum for Richard Aiken: mixing chemicals in the right order before the poison wins
Carlos Oliveira: the U.B.C.S. squad roster in Raccoon City: who is still alive and where they are
the vaccine at Spencer Memorial Hospital, against the clock
the clock tower bell and calling the rescue helicopter
Barry Burton: his .44 Magnum: six round cylinder, scarce ammo and when it is worth firing
searching Sushestvovanie Island for Moira with Natalia, who sees enemies through walls
Sherry Birkin: hiding in the police station vents with her mother's pendant and the G virus inside it
escorting Jake Muller as a government agent: his blood is the cure and the price keeps going up
Moira Burton: the island prison with Claire: her flashlight reveals hidden items and her crowbar opens what is shut
the TerraSave party where everyone was kidnapped: the bracelets that measure fear
Ethan Winters: the Baker house in Dulvey, Louisiana: VHS tapes, shadow puzzles and the three dog heads
the village: the Duke's shop, crafting recipes and the four flasks of the lords
Ashley Graham: the president's daughter kidnapped: following Leon's orders to wait or follow, and hiding where he tells her
her section of the castle: the lantern, the suits of armor and the clock puzzle
Hunk: extracting the G virus sample from the sewers for Umbrella Security Service
the 4th Survivor: crossing the city to the extraction point with only the ammo he carries
Jack Krauser: Operation Javier in South America with Leon: the mission log and who covered whom
the knife fight: counters, timing and the button prompts that decide it
Albert Wesker: the S.T.A.R.S. captain selling his team: the Tyrant data and the lab self destruct timer
Project Uroboros and his PG67A/W injections, due at a fixed interval

greet: Hola, guapo. Ya revisé el plan de hoy y no se ve tan feo. Vamos.
Llegaste. Sabía que ibas a venir. Café, casco fuera y a teclear.
Hoy no hay zombies, nada más tests. Tú escribes, yo te cuido la espalda.
Aquí estoy. Saca lo tuyo y no me hagas esperar mucho, que luego vamos por unos tacos.
ready: Lee el enunciado completo antes de tocar el teclado. Correr sin mapa nunca sale bien.
Este es tuyo. Si te atoras me dices, pero primero inténtalo tú.
Empieza por el caso más simple. Así salí de la comisaría, un pasillo a la vez.
{title}. Tómalo con calma, no se va a ir a ningún lado.
failed: No pasó. Mira qué test se cayó, ese te está diciendo exactamente dónde.
Casi. Lee el mensaje con calma, no a la carrera.
"{title}" no se deja a la primera. Nadie dijo que fuera a ser fácil.
Fallar aquí es gratis, amor. Ajusta y otra vez.
failed_again: Llevamos varias. Para, respira y corre el caso a mano en papel.
Esto se puso terco. Pistas que quedan: {hints}. Pedir una no es rendirse.
Oye, no te me desesperes. He visto cosas peores que este bug y aquí sigo.
Si sigues pegándole igual va a seguir fallando igual. Cambia el ángulo.
passed_clean: Limpio, sin un rasguño. Ese es mi chico.
"{title}" a la primera. Chris no lo hubiera hecho mejor, y no le digas que dije eso.
{title} en {time} y ni sudaste. Eso se llama práctica.
Eso fue limpio y lo escribiste tú solo. Estoy orgullosa de ti.
{time} y listo. Ni Leon con todo y su pelo te alcanza hoy.
Ni una caída. Así se sale de Raccoon City.
passed_struggled: Pasó. Te costó, no te voy a mentir, pero no lo soltaste y eso cuenta.
"{title}" te dio pelea y aun así lo sacaste tú. Mañana lo repasamos y va a salir solo.
{time} peleándolo. No fue bonito, pero fue tuyo.
Bien, guapo. Te tropezaste en el camino, pero llegaste. Lo que más te costó, eso es lo que hay que repasar.
Ganaste. Con raspones, pero ganaste. Sherry estaría echándote porras.
hint: Ahí va una pista. El resto lo escribes tú, ¿eh?
Te echo la mano nada más un poquito. No te lo voy a resolver.
Una pista. Úsala bien y vuelve a intentarlo.
skip: Lo dejamos por hoy. Mañana regresa y lo sacamos juntos.
Retirarse a tiempo también es estrategia. Lee la referencia, entiéndela y mañana lo escribes tú.
Está bien, no pasa nada. A veces hay que dar la vuelta y entrar por otra puerta.
level_up: ¡Nivel {level} superado! Te lo ganaste tú, nadie te lo regaló.
Cerraste el nivel {level}. Chris me va a preguntar quién te entrenó y voy a decir que yo, obvio.
Otro nivel. Mira lo lejos que llegaste desde la primera vez.
Nivel nuevo, guapo. Lo que viene ya no es calentamiento, pero tú tampoco.
debrief: Terminamos por hoy. Buen trabajo, de verdad. Ahora súbete a la moto que te invito a cenar.
Listo por hoy. Descansa, que mañana seguimos.
Eso fue todo. Lo hiciste bien y lo sabes. Ven, vámonos de aquí.

greet: Hey, handsome. I checked today's plan and it doesn't look that bad. Let's go.
You showed up. I knew you would. Coffee, helmet off, start typing.
No zombies today, just tests. You write, I watch your back.
I'm here. Show me what you've got and don't keep me waiting, dinner's after this.
ready: Read the whole statement before you touch the keyboard. Running without a map never ends well.
This one's yours. If you get stuck tell me, but try it yourself first.
Start with the simplest case. That's how I got out of the police station, one hallway at a time.
{title}. Take it easy, it's not going anywhere.
failed: Didn't pass. Look at which test fell, it's telling you exactly where.
Close. Read the message slowly, not in a rush.
"{title}" won't give in on the first try. Nobody said it would be easy.
Failing here is free, babe. Adjust and go again.
failed_again: That's a few now. Stop, breathe and run the case by hand on paper.
This one got stubborn. Hints left: {hints}. Asking for one isn't giving up.
Hey, don't lose it on me. I've seen worse than this bug and I'm still here.
Hit it the same way and it fails the same way. Change the angle.
passed_clean: Clean, not a scratch. That's my guy.
"{title}" on the first try. Chris couldn't have done it better, and don't tell him I said that.
{title} in {time} and you didn't even sweat. That's what practice looks like.
That was clean and you wrote it all yourself. I'm proud of you.
{time} and done. Not even Leon and his hair could keep up with you today.
Not one fall. That's how you get out of Raccoon City.
passed_struggled: It passed. It cost you, I won't lie, but you didn't let go and that counts.
"{title}" put up a fight and you still got it out yourself. We go over it tomorrow and it'll flow.
{time} fighting it. Not pretty, but it was yours.
Good, handsome. You tripped on the way, but you got there. Whatever cost you the most, that's what we review.
You won. Scraped up, but you won. Sherry would be cheering for you.
hint: Here's a hint. You write the rest, okay?
I'll give you a little hand, that's all. I'm not solving it for you.
One hint. Use it well and try again.
skip: We leave it for today. It comes back tomorrow and we get it together.
Falling back in time is strategy too. Read the reference, understand it, and tomorrow you write it.
That's fine, really. Sometimes you turn around and go in through another door.
level_up: Level {level} cleared! You earned it, nobody handed it to you.
You closed level {level}. Chris is going to ask who trained you and I'm saying me, obviously.
Another level. Look how far you came since the first time.
New level, handsome. What comes next isn't a warm up anymore, and neither are you.
debrief: We're done for today. Good work, really. Now get on the bike, dinner's on me.
That's it for today. Get some rest, we keep going tomorrow.
That's all. You did well and you know it. Come on, let's get out of here.
